## Three flowers, two measurements

The iris dataset, seen through its petals.

**25 October 2026** · Mohammad Aman Hayat

:::

::: {.slide}

## A small dataset with a clear question

The built-in `iris` dataset records four measurements for **150 flowers**, split equally across three species. Can two petal measurements separate them?

**150** flowers &nbsp;&nbsp; **3** species &nbsp;&nbsp; **2** petal measurements in this view

:::

::: {.slide}

## Explore the petals

Hover to inspect a flower. Click a species in the legend to show or hide it. Drag to zoom; double-click to reset.

```{r plotly-iris, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(plotly)

colors <- c(setosa = "#52d6b5", versicolor = "#ffae70", virginica = "#a78bfa")
p <- plot_ly()
for (species in levels(iris$Species)) {
  flowers <- iris[iris$Species == species, ]
  p <- add_markers(
    p,
    x = flowers$Petal.Length, y = flowers$Petal.Width,
    name = species, marker = list(color = colors[[species]], size = 11,
                                   opacity = 0.78, line = list(color = "#17233b", width = 0.6)),
    text = paste0("<b>", species, "</b><br>Petal length: ", flowers$Petal.Length,
                  " cm<br>Petal width: ", flowers$Petal.Width, " cm"),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  )
}
p <- layout(
  p, paper_bgcolor = "#111b30", plot_bgcolor = "#111b30",
  font = list(color = "#eaf0fb", family = "Arial"),
  xaxis = list(title = "Petal length (cm)", gridcolor = "#29374f", zeroline = FALSE),
  yaxis = list(title = "Petal width (cm)", gridcolor = "#29374f", zeroline = FALSE),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.15),
  margin = list(l = 65, r = 20, t = 54, b = 60)
)
config(p, displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

:::

::: {.slide}

## The pattern is in the petals

**Setosa stands apart.** Its petals occupy the lower-left cluster, while versicolor and virginica overlap near the middle.

Two measurements tell most of the story, but the overlap is a useful reminder: a scatterplot reveals ambiguity as well as separation.

Source: R's built-in `iris` dataset. Chart: Plotly for R.

:::
